articles.headline: OpenAI commits $1 billion to cyberdefense effort amid AI safety scrutiny
articles.summary: OpenAI pledged $1 billion in subsidized access to its AI cybersecurity tools, training and technical support for organizations protecting critical services. For businesses, this signals both rising AI-enabled cyber risk and a growing market for defensive automation, with implications for security budgets and vendor selection.

articles.headline: TSMC says it still cannot keep pace with AI boom despite fivefold capacity expansion
articles.summary: TSMC said it is expanding capacity sharply but remains unable to satisfy booming AI demand. For companies buying chips, cloud infrastructure or AI services, this suggests continued supply pressure, elevated pricing and longer planning horizons for hardware and compute procurement.

articles.headline: EU starts using new powers to send AI information requests to dozens of companies
articles.summary: The European Union began using new powers to request information from companies after incidents this summer highlighted AI risks. Businesses deploying or selling AI in Europe may face more compliance work, documentation demands and potential scrutiny over model safety and governance.
